findings.evidence: "Also, the benefits team reviews the reimbursement log on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Remove "Also," and restructure to: "The benefits team also reviews the reimbursement log on the first business day of the month."
findings.violation: Starting the sentence with "Also," is awkward and creates redundancy with the preceding sentence about the benefits team's activities.

findings.evidence: "Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing."
findings.fix: Restructure as: "After the manager signs the request and finance confirms the budget line, the stipend request moves to final processing."
findings.location: How to Apply section, second paragraph
findings.violation: The sentence awkwardly starts with "Also," and contains confusing nested conditions that make the approval sequence unclear.

findings.evidence: "The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the summary review happens before submission to processing or if this is a post-completion verification step.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: The process sequence is unclear - if processing has already finished and a confirmation email was sent, the employee should not be submitting a "final request" afterwards.

findings.evidence: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives."
findings.fix: Change to: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing information is provided."
findings.violation: "Missing item" is vague; this should refer to missing documentation or information, not a physical item.

findings.evidence: "Employees keep proof of purchase for every stipend item. A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Clarify the documentation requirements: either a photo is acceptable for all requests or specify which scenarios require the full receipt.
findings.violation: These statements contradict each other - it's unclear whether a photo is sufficient for all requests or only some, and whether it satisfies the retention requirement.

findings.evidence: "The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year."
findings.fix: Change to: "The stipend pays up to $500 per benefit year."
findings.violation: Currency formatting is not professional - should use "$500" rather than spelling out "dollars" with a numeral.

findings.evidence: "Also, unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year."
findings.fix: Remove "Also," or restructure to: "Unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year."
findings.violation: Starting the sentence with "Also," is awkward.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Use consistent perspective: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the company may request a brief photo verification once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first paragraph
findings.violation: Inconsistent pronouns shift from "you" (the employee) to "we" (the company), creating confusion about responsibility.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly," and begin with: "The policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph
findings.violation: "Similarly" does not logically connect to the previous sentence about equipment condition checks.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days."
findings.fix: Identify the roles explicitly and rewrite with consistent perspective for each step, specifying the responsible party.
findings.violation: This section uses "you" inconsistently without clarifying whether it addresses the employee, manager, or administrator. "Countersign" is unclear about who performs this action.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: Awkward grammar - "and the uploaded receipt" is not parallel with "confirming eligibility."

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence from Special Cases.
findings.violation: This sentence is an exact repetition of text from the Program Overview section.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Remove the three unrelated sentences; keep only the first sentence about benefit team coordination.
findings.violation: The second, third, and fourth sentences are completely unrelated to the stipend program and do not belong in this section.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify: "The finance office also flags any request from the same employee for the same equipment category within the same quarter."
findings.violation: "Repeats" is ambiguous - it is unclear whether this refers to the same employee requesting twice, the same equipment category, or another condition.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Change to: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over $200 before it pays out."
findings.violation: Currency formatting should be consistent and professional - should use "$200" rather than spelling out "dollars" with a numeral.

findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence from Questions and Updates.
findings.location: Questions and Updates section, second sentence
findings.violation: This sentence is an exact repetition from the Program Overview section.
